title: Neither live BatchNFTMinter instance has a pauser, so the contract's own documented recovery procedure cannot be executed
description: Read-only mainnet verification found `pauser() == address(0)` and `paused() == false` on BOTH `0x81896F48…` (RatchetBatchNFTMinter) and `0x86866e01…` — and `0x86866e01…` is the instance actually holding 219.99 USDC as an intended, gated bounty. The contract's own NatSpec says `rescueERC20` is 'a race the owner will usually lose' and that 'pause first, then rescue' is the only dependable sequence, which is UNAVAILABLE when `pauser == 0`.
impact: No direct loss. The documented break-glass for CLASS-002 and CLASS-007 is currently unexecutable on BOTH deployed instances. 0x86866e01… holds 219.99 USDC as an intended, gated bounty with no dependable recovery path.
attackPath: 1. pauser() == address(0) and paused() == false on BOTH 0x81896F48… and 0x86866e01… (read-only mainnet, block 25572875).
2. The contract's NatSpec states rescueERC20 is 'a race the owner will usually lose' and that 'pause first, then rescue' is the only dependable sequence.
3. pause() is onlyPauser, so with pauser == 0 the sequence cannot be run.
4. Any recovery attempt degrades to the race the NatSpec says the owner loses.
likelihood: n/a — this is a present, verified state, not a probability.
justification: QA/Low: the absence of a mitigation is not itself a loss, and the fix is a single owner transaction. Deliberately NOT escalated to Medium — no assets move as a consequence of this finding alone. It is filed at Low rather than QA because it is LIVE ON MAINNET and it falsifies the escape-hatch premise that a prior suppression of the adjacent sweep rested on (declinedSuppressions, DEDUP-20-002).

footgunFraming: Law-3 NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun. Law-3 test: 'would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised?' YES — the contract's OWN NatSpec prescribes 'pause first, then rescue' as the only dependable recovery sequence, and nothing in the deploy script or NatSpec flags that the procedure silently becomes inexecutable when the pauser slot is left unset. DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:38 even lists 'unset pauser' as an expected INTERMEDIATE state. No malicious-owner vector is asserted.
